title.value: On the Expressivity of Markov Reward (Extended Abstract)
title.justification: The title is provided at the start of the document, following the conference information.
title.quote: On the Expressivity of Markov Reward (Extended Abstract)

analysis.description: The paper examines the ability of Markov reward functions to express different types of tasks in reinforcement learning, framed as sets of acceptable behaviors, partial orderings over behaviors, and partial orderings over trajectories. It proves that some tasks cannot be realized by Markov reward functions and presents algorithms to determine and construct reward functions when possible.

type.justification: The paper presents theoretical results regarding the expressivity of Markov reward functions, rather than empirical study or experiments on models or data.
type.quote: Our main results prove that while reward can express many of these tasks, there exist instances of each task type that no Markov reward function can capture.

name.justification: The research focuses on the expressivity of reward signals, which are central in reinforcement learning paradigms.
name.quote: The reinforcement-learning (RL) problem puts the study of such agents front and center under the assumption that we focus on agents that learn to maximize reward.

name.justification: The study is framed around finite Markov Decision Processes (MDPs), which is a subfield of reinforcement learning.
name.quote: Concretely, we consider three kinds of task in the context of finite Markov Decision Processes (MDPs)

name.justification: The research explores different abstract notions of tasks in reinforcement learning.
name.quote: We frame this study around three new abstract notions of “task”: (1) a set of acceptable behaviors, (2) a partial ordering over behaviors, or (3) a partial ordering over trajectories.
